text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that can understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites, and articles. Users can improve results through prompt engineering, which means writing clear and specific instructions. LLMs are very useful for tasks like writing, translating, and answering questions. However, they also have limits: they can make mistakes, sometimes produce false information, and may reflect biases found in their training data. For these reasons, it is important to check their answers carefully.
